government.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
government.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

government.title: Blame Avoidance and Corruption: How Politicians' Denials Shape Citizen Perceptions and Political Accountability
government.short_title: Blame Avoidance and Corruption: How Politicians' Denials Shape Citizen Perceptions and Politic…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how politicians accused of corruption respond when they deny their wrongdoing. The research shows that when politicians say they are innocent or blame others for their actions, it can improve their image and chances of winning elections. This is especially true for people who strongly support one political party. Understanding this helps us see how leaders influence public opinion about corruption in politics.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bilan d’une recherche immersive en Police Judiciaire française
government.short_title: Le facteur émotionnel de l’activité : analyser les « angles morts » pour améliorer la QVCT. Bi…
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on understanding the emotional risks in police work and how they manage their emotions to improve job satisfaction. It was conducted by observing various police units like forensic science, digital investigation, financial division, criminal division, anti-terrorism unit, and more over 26 days. The study found two key emotions that are hard for them to express: interest and frustration. These emotions make it difficult for officers to discuss their work-related feelings openly, leading to invisible or undiscussed labor.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.title: International Anti-Corruption Commissions: Explaining Institutional Design and Autonomy
government.short_title: International Anti-Corruption Commissions: Explaining Institutional Design and Autonomy
government.plain_summary: Political corruption is a big problem that governments often struggle with and sometimes use anti-corruption measures against their own democracy. International Anti-Corruption Commissions (IACCs) help address this issue by working with both international experts and local people. Some IACCs have more independence than others, which can affect how effective they are in fighting corruption. In places like northern Central America, when there are coalitions that include government insiders and activists at the table during negotiations, these groups use their influence to make sure anti-corruption efforts don't undermine democracy too much.

government.title: Diagnostic Significance of Combining Anti-Gliadin IgA and Anti-Tissue Transglutaminase IgA in Suspected Celiac Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study
government.short_title: Diagnostic Significance of Combining Anti-Gliadin IgA and Anti-Tissue Transglutaminase IgA in…
government.plain_summary: This study looked at a group of 384 people who might have Celiac Disease. They tested these people for two antibodies: one against gliadin (anti-gliadin IgA) and another against tissue transglutaminase (anti-tTG IgA). About 13% had the anti-gliadin antibody, while about 15% had the anti-tTG antibody. When both were positive in some people, it was more common than just one being positive.

government.title: Valuation Methods for Assessing Government-Owned Heritage Buildings in Malaysia
government.short_title: Valuation Methods for Assessing Government-Owned Heritage Buildings in Malaysia
government.source: IPN Journal of Research and Practice in Public Sector Accounting and Management
government.plain_summary: This study aimed to find suitable methods for valuing government-owned historic buildings in Malaysia. It used focus group discussions with experts from various fields like architecture and conservation. The research concluded that these buildings should be valued using a cost approach, focusing on their reproduction costs rather than assigning them a low value of RM1. This ensures compliance with the Malaysian Public Sector Accounting Standards (MPSAS).

government.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Transparency, and Public Service Delivery
government.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Tran…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how artificial intelligence is being used in government services. It found that while AI can speed up service delivery and improve monitoring of processes, it also creates issues like unclear responsibility for decisions made by AI systems, lack of transparency about these decisions, uneven readiness among staff to use AI, and risks to human decision-making. To address these challenges, the study recommends creating clear guidelines on accountability, making AI explanations transparent, encouraging public disclosure, ensuring human oversight over AI processes, providing training for staff, and offering ways for citizens to appeal if they have concerns about AI decisions.

government.title: Beyond Compliance: Building Financial and Anti-Fraud Resilience in the Digital Economy
government.short_title: Beyond Compliance: Building Financial and Anti-Fraud Resilience in the Digital Economy
government.plain_summary: Building financial and anti-fraud resilience is crucial for organizations to maintain stability and public trust in a digital economy. Fraud has evolved into sophisticated forms like cyber-enabled fraud, identity theft, and cryptocurrency scams, requiring more than just compliance measures. To prevent, detect, respond to, and recover from these threats, institutions need integrated governance, control systems, intelligence gathering, response mechanisms, and learning processes. Effective resilience includes board oversight, strong authentication, internal controls, transaction monitoring, whistleblower channels, anti-money laundering integration, incident response plans, customer protection, and post-incident reviews.

government.title: From Corruption to Declining Public Trust: Implications for Political Participation in West Aceh Regency
government.short_title: From Corruption to Declining Public Trust: Implications for Political Participation in West Ac…
government.plain_summary: Corruption significantly impacts the level of public trust in West Aceh Regency's governance, affecting both elected and non-elected institutions. Citizens view corruption as a lack of accountability and transparency, using public resources unfairly. This perception leads to declining trust in government bodies. To improve this situation, it’s important to strengthen formal accountability, transparency, and oversight mechanisms.

government.title: The Defects of "Zeroing" in WTO Anti-Dumping Agreement and Legislative Amendment
government.short_title: The Defects of "Zeroing" in WTO Anti-Dumping Agreement and Legislative Amendment
government.source: Lecture Notes in Education Psychology and Public Media
government.plain_summary: Zeroing is a controversial practice in World Trade Organization (WTO) anti-dumping laws where authorities set negative dumping margins to zero when calculating overall dumping rates. This artificially inflates final duty rates. The WTO Appellate Body has ruled this inconsistent with core provisions of the Anti-Dumping Agreement, but it still persists due to legal ambiguities and protectionist incentives. To address these issues, there should be clear prohibitions, standardized calculation methods, and stronger enforcement mechanisms in legislation.

government.title: The Judiciary and the Anti-Corruption Bloc: Transformations in Wartime
government.short_title: The Judiciary and the Anti-Corruption Bloc: Transformations in Wartime
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how Ukraine is transforming its judicial and anti-corruption systems during wartime. The main focus is on reforms aimed at reducing political influence in key institutions like the High Qualification Commission for Judges and the High Council of Justice. It also highlights efforts to strengthen the anti-corruption bloc by giving the State Anti-Corruption Program a separate legal status, requiring public officials to declare their assets, and implementing an electronic system for criminal proceedings. Practitioners should understand these changes are crucial for maintaining fair trials and preventing corruption during wartime, but they must also address personnel issues like hiring honest judges and prosecutors through transparent processes.

government.title: Fostering Public Trust and Accountability in Public Healthcare: The Role of Transparency, Integrity, and Independence in Internal Audit Governance
government.short_title: Fostering Public Trust and Accountability in Public Healthcare: The Role of Transparency, Inte…
government.source: European Journal of Social Science Education and Research
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how transparency, independence, and integrity help improve internal audits in public healthcare. It found that having clear information and being free from bias are important for good audits. However, strong ethical values alone don't make a big difference to audit quality. Instead, they play a crucial role when there is also trust and fairness in the system.

government.title: Influence of Artificial Intelligence Adoption on Employee Productivity in the Public Sector: A Case of SMC 460/2026 Participants at Kenya School of Government Lower Kabete Campus
government.short_title: Influence of Artificial Intelligence Adoption on Employee Productivity in the Public Sector: A…
government.plain_summary: This study looked at how using artificial intelligence (AI) helps government workers do their jobs better in a specific program for new public servants. They found that most participants used AI tools like ChatGPT to help with writing and research. The use of these tools improved the quality of reports, saved time by reducing manual work, and helped manage workload more efficiently. However, there was room for improvement such as clear guidelines, proper training, and ensuring privacy.

government.title: Public Procurement's Long COVID : Emergency Responses and Shifting Corruption Risks in Europe
government.short_title: Public Procurement's Long COVID : Emergency Responses and Shifting Corruption Risks in Europe
government.plain_summary: This study examines how the public procurement system in Europe was affected during the pandemic. It found that spending on coronavirus-related projects led to an increase in corruption risks, especially in countries where government controls are not very strict. This happened because new companies without experience dealing with COVID-19 products took advantage of weak regulations to win big contracts. The study also noted that this increased risk spread beyond just healthcare procurement into other areas like general public services.

government.title: Teacher Engagement in Education for Sustainability: Integrating Anti-Corruption Values into Learning in Remote Areas
government.short_title: Teacher Engagement in Education for Sustainability: Integrating Anti-Corruption Values into Le…
government.source: Journal of Moral and Civic Education
government.plain_summary: This research focuses on how teachers can better integrate anti-corruption values into their lessons, especially in remote areas where resources are limited. It found that effective teacher engagement is key, involving readiness to understand anti-corruption concepts, supportive school environments, appropriate teaching methods, and fostering students' integrity development. The study proposes a framework for teachers to help them engage more effectively with these goals, which can be applied to improve education in remote schools. This practical approach helps ensure that even in challenging settings, children learn about important values like honesty and fairness.

government.title: Nursing students' perceptions of an anti-stigma intervention for schizophrenia: a qualitative focus group study
government.short_title: Nursing students' perceptions of an anti-stigma intervention for schizophrenia: a qualitative…
government.plain_summary: This study aimed to understand how nursing students felt about a program designed to reduce stigma around schizophrenia. It found that participating in this program was seen as easy to do, helpful for people who need it, and effective at changing attitudes. The students also gave suggestions on how the program could be made even better. This information can help make future programs more useful for health professionals like nurses.

government.title: PUBLIC SECTOR AUDIT AND FRAUD DETECTION IN NIGERIA: THE MODERATING ROLE OF TECHNOLOGY
government.short_title: PUBLIC SECTOR AUDIT AND FRAUD DETECTION IN NIGERIA: THE MODERATING ROLE OF TECHNOLOGY
government.source: International Journal of Accounting, Management and Economic Review
government.plain_summary: This research looked at how audits conducted by the government help catch scams in Nigeria's ministries. It found that regular financial, compliance, and special audits are important for preventing things like theft of assets or payroll errors. The study also showed that using technology to do these audits makes them even more effective. So, if governments improve their auditing practices and use more tech tools, they can spot fraud better and keep public money safer from being stolen.

government.title: From denial to accountability: Co-evolution of government communication and public sentiment in a social-mediated crisis in China
government.short_title: From denial to accountability: Co-evolution of government communication and public sentiment i…
government.source: Journal of Asian and African Studies
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how China's government communicated during a big incident involving a woman in 2022. It found that as the government started admitting mistakes instead of denying them, people’s feelings about it improved slightly but stayed negative overall. The study shows that when the government is honest and transparent, it can help improve public trust over time. This research helps governments understand how to better communicate during crises by considering what people expect from them.

government.title: Innovation entry as governance filter: shaping exploratory digital innovation in the public sector
government.short_title: Innovation entry as governance filter: shaping exploratory digital innovation in the public se…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how the way government organizations handle new ideas affects their ability to try out innovative technologies and approaches. Many public sector groups are used to solving problems step-by-step, but this can make it hard to explore new ideas freely. The research found that the rules for starting and moving through innovation projects act like filters, often pushing exploratory work towards more traditional ways of working. This means they tend to focus on quick fixes rather than experimenting with different solutions.

government.title: E-Government to Combat Corruption Worldwide: Dominant Factors and a Holistic Model Emerging From Structured Literature Review

government.title: How ethical leadership reduces corruption in Pakistan’s public sector: job satisfaction as a mediator
government.short_title: How ethical leadership reduces corruption in Pakistan’s public sector: job satisfaction as a m…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how ethical leadership can reduce corruption among public employees in Pakistan. It found that when leaders are ethical, it leads to higher job satisfaction for their staff. Higher job satisfaction then reduces the likelihood of corruption by making workers feel more committed to serving the public. This study suggests that if managers promote ethical behavior and boost employee happiness, they can help prevent corrupt practices in government.

government.title: Ethical and Legal Implications of AI-Driven Anti-Corruption Technologies in Developing Democracies
government.short_title: Ethical and Legal Implications of AI-Driven Anti-Corruption Technologies in Developing Democra…
government.source: African Journal of Law Political Research and Administration
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how AI can help spot fraud in government spending in countries that are just starting to have democratic systems. It suggests that using AI like machine learning could make it easier for people to see if money is being spent unfairly or wasted. However, there are still big challenges like not having enough good data or fair rules. The main idea is that while AI can be useful, it needs to work with human checks and balances to really help stop corruption.

government.title: Corruption and the Composition of Business Activity in Brazil
government.short_title: Corruption and the Composition of Business Activity in Brazil
government.plain_summary: Corruption affects how businesses are distributed across different industries. In Brazil, areas with higher levels of corruption tend to have fewer jobs and business establishments in sectors like construction and manufacturing. Instead, there's a larger presence of agricultural activities. The study also found that where corruption is more prevalent, the competition among businesses becomes tighter or less competitive depending on the sector.

government.title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
government.short_title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
government.source: Journal of Social Politics and Governance (JSPG)
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how different groups like governments, businesses, non-profits, schools, and media work together to fight corruption using something called the Pentahelix framework. It found that for effective anti-corruption efforts, these groups need to collaborate closely rather than working separately. The Pentahelix model shows they can tackle corruption more effectively when they all play a part in it. This collaborative approach is key to creating strong systems against corruption and making sure it doesn't happen anymore.

government.title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA)
government.short_title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering…
government.plain_summary: Money laundering is a significant threat affecting competitive markets, security, and consumer well-being. The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA) was created as part of new EU regulations to improve supervisory standards and coordinate the fight against illicit finance across Europe. AMLA combines classification functions like setting rules and standards with selective enforcement tools such as direct supervision of high-risk groups and escalation mechanisms. By viewing these aspects through a collective-action lens, it helps explain how AMLA can effectively police money laundering while also highlighting its limitations in fully addressing the issue.

government.title: The Challenges of Implementing E-government in the Public Sector: A Case Study on The Gambia
government.short_title: The Challenges of Implementing E-government in the Public Sector: A Case Study on The Gambia
government.plain_summary: E-government has become a way for governments to deliver services more efficiently and make governance transparent. However, implementing it can be challenging, especially in developing countries with limited resources. A case study from The Gambia found that while e-government helps improve service delivery, transparency, accountability, and citizen participation, there are still big hurdles like not having enough IT infrastructure or skilled employees to use digital tools effectively. There's also a lack of collaboration between different government departments and issues related to internet access and trust in government services.

government.title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesian Governance
government.short_title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesi…
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how ethics, accountability, and transparency work together in Indonesian government systems. It found that even with digitalization efforts, if there isn't a strong enough foundation of ethics, these measures can fail to prevent corruption and lose public trust. The research suggests integrating ethical practices, making information transparent, and ensuring accountability are all important for effective governance. By combining these elements, Indonesia can improve its government systems and build more trustworthy relationships with the people it serves.

government.title: Unethical leadership in the South African public sector tender processes through the lens of game theory
government.short_title: Unethical leadership in the South African public sector tender processes through the lens of g…

government.title: CHALLENGES AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF UKRAINE’S STATE ANTI-CORRUPTION BODIES
government.short_title: CHALLENGES AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF UKRAINE’S STATE ANTI-CORRUPTION B…
government.plain_summary: This article discusses key issues facing Ukraine's anti-corruption bodies and suggests ways to improve their effectiveness. Challenges include fragmented legal support, political instability, lack of coordination among agencies, limited resources, unclear jurisdictional powers, and low public trust. To address these, the Ukrainian government should focus on strengthening institutional independence, optimizing power distribution, improving human resources, enhancing coordination mechanisms, and increasing transparency in sensitive areas like procurement and financial controls. These steps are crucial for building trust with society and aligning anti-corruption efforts with European standards of governance.

government.title: Distinguishing Transparency and Accountability as Separate Pillars of Good Governance
government.short_title: Distinguishing Transparency and Accountability as Separate Pillars of Good Governance
government.source: Africa Journal of Public Sector Development and Governance

government.title: Working Paper 60: Understanding the enemy
government.short_title: Working Paper 60: Understanding the enemy
government.source: Basel Institute on Governance Working Papers
government.plain_summary: This working paper discusses how corruption is not just about individual bad behavior but a networked issue involving social, economic, and political interactions. Understanding these networks can help in fighting corruption more effectively by seeing how they function across different levels of society. By looking at the structures and norms that support corrupt activities, we can develop better strategies to combat it. The paper suggests that anti-corruption efforts should learn from informal networks' positive aspects, making them a useful model for new initiatives.

government.title: The Impact of Corruption on Biodiversity Conservation in Nigeria: A Review of Some Critical Issues
government.short_title: The Impact of Corruption on Biodiversity Conservation in Nigeria: A Review of Some Critical Is…
government.source: International Journal of Governance and Public Policy Analysis
government.plain_summary: Corruption has significantly worsened the crisis of biodiversity loss and environmental degradation in Nigeria. It includes theft, bribery, fraud, abuse of power, and other unethical practices that harm natural resources like forests, wildlife habitats, and water bodies. This corruption leads to overexploitation of resources, deforestation, poaching, pollution, and many more issues. To address this crisis, reforms are needed in governance, legal systems, and institutions.

government.title: Integrity disclosure as an anti-fraud strategy: Evidence from local government websites in developing countries
government.short_title: Integrity disclosure as an anti-fraud strategy: Evidence from local government websites in dev…
government.plain_summary: Corruption continues to be a significant issue in Indonesian governance, affecting public trust and service effectiveness. To combat this, governments are encouraged to disclose information about their operations openly. A study analyzed how 29 regencies and six cities in Central Java Province disclosed government integrity on their websites using the Integrity Framework Disclosure Index (IFDI). The IFDI includes categories like risk assessments, policies, and procedures.

nonprofit.title: The Ethics of Islamic Philanthropy
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study about Islamic philanthropy uses Quranic teachings to understand the ethics behind giving. It identifies four key principles: being responsible (amanah), improving oneself (tazkiyah), sharing with others in cycles (dawr), and giving back as a way of receiving (mukāfa’ah). These principles form a strong moral foundation for Islamic charity, showing it's not just about voluntary acts but also includes duties. This research helps clarify how these ethical guidelines affect the structure and diversity within nonprofit organizations.
